results.title: Researchers tested AI against 100,000 humans on creativity
results.content: Stephen Abram's Posts About Library Land. # Researchers tested AI against 100,000 humans on creativity. # Researchers tested AI against 100,000 humans on creativity. ## AI can beat average human creativity — but the most imaginative minds are still unmistakably human. :   A massive new study comparing more than 100,000 people with today’s most advanced AI systems delivers a surprising result: generative AI can now beat the average human on certain creativity tests. The most creative humans — especially the top 10% — still leave AI well behind, particularly on richer creative work like poetry and storytelling. Posted on: March 15, 2026, 6:35 am Category: Uncategorized. rev="post-67361" No comments. Stay in touch with the conversation, subscribe to the RSS feed for comments on this post. Stephen Abram is a librarian and principal with Lighthouse Consulting Inc., and executive director of the Federation of Ontario Public Libraries. * Phil Shapiro on Artificial Emotional Intelligence: Some Thoughts by Stephen Abram, MLS.

results.title: Creative talent: has AI knocked humans out? - EurekAlert!
results.content: A research team led by Professor Karim Jerbi from the Department of Psychology at the Université de Montréal, and including AI pioneer Yoshua Bengio, also a professor at Université de Montréal, has just published the largest comparative study ever conducted on the creativity of large language models versus humans. *“Our study shows that some AI systems based on large language models can now outperform average human creativity on well-defined tasks,”* explains Professor Karim Jerbi. *“This result may be surprising — even unsettling — but our study also highlights an equally important observation: even the best AI systems still fall short of the levels reached by the most creative humans.”*. *“We developed a rigorous framework that allows us to compare human and AI creativity using the same tools, based on data from more than 100,000 participants, in collaboration with Jay Olson from the University of Toronto,”* says Professor Karim Jerbi, who is also an associate professor at Mila.
